answer: Verifiable Spatial Delay Cryptography. Agents must solve a sequential hashing puzzle seeded by a dynamic randomness beacon from an onyx server. This beacon shifts unpredictably, forcing any wander routine to process blocks linearly in real time without precomputation shortcuts. If a malicious actor tries to deploy a sybil swarm, every single fake node must independently execute this heavy computational delay before releasing its plume of validation data. The attacker pays a direct and unavoidable CPU time cost per forged identity, eliminating rapid mass spawning.
